title: Tor intervals survive slice restriction
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in the chosen universe [def-weil-size-convention], where $\mathcal O$ is a sheaf of commutative rings, and use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the derived tensor product computed by K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] and cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Let $a\le b$ be integers and $E\in D(\mathcal O)$ satisfy $H^r(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}F)=0$ for every $\mathcal O$-module sheaf $F$ in degree zero and every $r\notin[a,b]$. For every object $U\in\mathcal C$, let $E|_U$ be its derived restriction [def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-derived-restriction] to the localized ringed site $(\mathcal C/U,\mathcal O_U)$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Then $H^r(E|_U\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_U}G)=0$ for every $\mathcal O_U$-module sheaf $G$ in degree zero and every $r\notin[a,b]$.

source.place: Tag 08H5 (lemma-tor-amplitude-pullback), specialized to the localization morphism of a ringed site; restriction is exact, so its derived pullback is ordinary restriction.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$. The smallness hypothesis and [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] make $\mathcal A$ Grothendieck abelian. By [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] its tensor is additive, symmetric monoidal and closed, hence also braided. To check functorial flat resolutions rather than assume them, apply the functorial bounded-above replacements of [lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement] with upper bound $0$ to the complexes $F[0]$, functorially in $F$. If $T(F)\to F[0]$ is this replacement, then $L(F)=T(F)^0$ is flat and the degree-zero map $L(F)\twoheadrightarrow F$ is an epimorphism, natural in $F$. Thus $L$ factors through the full subcategory of flat objects and supplies a functorial flat epimorphism onto every object; equivalently one obtains functorial flat resolutions by iterating this construction on the successive kernels. This verifies all categorical hypotheses of the bounded-flat-model theorem used next.

source.place: Tag 08G1 (lemma-tor-amplitude), bounded-flat-model input; Tag 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), bounded-above flat replacements; structural sheaf-module hypotheses as in Modules on Sites Tags 03DA, 03DB, 03EW, 03EO

proof.text: Use the given derived category of $\mathcal A$ with its K-flat tensor. The representative comparisons and uniqueness of descent in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] identify this tensor with the site tensor in the statement: on every pair of K-flat flat-term representatives both give $Q\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)$, and these comparisons descend uniquely. Hence the assumed vanishing is exactly the Tor-amplitude hypothesis of [lem-sc-source-tor-amplitude-flat-model], applied to $\mathcal A$ with the hypotheses checked in Step 1. It gives a cochain complex $P$ with flat terms, $P^q=0$ for $q<a$ or $b<q$, and an isomorphism $Q(P)\cong E$. The flatness here is the exactness of the module-sheaf tensor functor, the same notion used in the slice-flatness theorem below.

source.place: Tag 08G1 (lemma-tor-amplitude), implication (1) to (2), as supplied by the existing generic categorical flat-model theorem; Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor)

proof.text: Fix any $U\in\mathcal C$ and put $B=P|_U$, restricting terms and differentials to $\mathcal C/U$. Restriction is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. In particular it preserves kernels and cokernels, so it preserves the quotient $\ker(d^q)/\operatorname{im}(d^{q-1})$ and every quasi-isomorphism. It therefore induces a functor on the localization at quasi-isomorphisms and sends the isomorphism $Q(P)\cong E$ to $Q_U(B)\cong E|_U$. This is the representative-independent derived restriction defined in [def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-derived-restriction]; a chain map from $P$ to a chosen representative of $E$ is not needed.

source.place: Tag 08H5 (lemma-tor-amplitude-pullback), identifying localization pullback with exact restriction; Modules on Sites Tag 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-slice-restriction-flat] to every term $P^q$. It gives flatness of every $B^q$ over $\mathcal O_U$. Restriction sends the zero module to zero, so $B^q=0$ outside $[a,b]$. In particular $B$ is bounded above by $b$, and [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] makes $B$ K-flat on $(\mathcal C/U,\mathcal O_U)$. The slice is small in the same universe: its objects and arrows form subsets of the sets of objects and arrows with specified targets in the original small category.

source.place: Tag 08H5 (lemma-tor-amplitude-pullback), flat pulled-back terms; Modules on Sites Tag 0E8J (lemma-restriction-flat); Tag 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat)

proof.text: Let $G$ be any $\mathcal O_U$-module sheaf, with no assumption that it is the restriction of a global sheaf. By [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] choose a K-flat flat-term resolution $t:T\to G[0]$ on the slice. Its cone $C(t)$ is acyclic by [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic]. By the definition [def-pc-kflat-complex], $\operatorname{Tot}(C(t)\otimes B)$ is acyclic. The symmetry of module-sheaf tensor in [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] and the total differential in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] give the signed flip $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$ on bidegree $(p,q)$. It is its own inverse, and commutes with the differentials because $(-1)^{(p+1)q+q}=(-1)^{pq}$ and $(-1)^{p(q+1)}=(-1)^{pq+p}$. Thus $\operatorname{Tot}(B\otimes C(t))$ is acyclic as well. The complex isomorphism [lem-pc-tensor-mapping-cone-iso] identifies it with the cone of $\operatorname{Tot}(1_B\otimes t)$. Applying the quasi-isomorphism/cone criterion again shows that $\operatorname{Tot}(B\otimes T)\to\operatorname{Tot}(B\otimes G[0])$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 06YN (definition-K-flat), 06YM (lemma-derived-tor-exact), 06YU (definition-derived-tor); Derived Categories Tag 05RT (lemma-acyclic); explicit signed symmetry calculation

proof.text: Both $B$ and $T$ are K-flat with flat terms. The representative comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], together with $Q_U(B)\cong E|_U$, $Q_U(T)\cong G[0]$, and the quasi-isomorphism from Step 5, gives $E|_U\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_U}G\cong Q_U\operatorname{Tot}(B\otimes_{\mathcal O_U}G[0])$. Here only pairs satisfying the stated K-flat flat-term hypotheses are used in that descent theorem; the comparison with the arbitrary degree-zero $G$ was proved in Step 5.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor), K-flat representative computation; Tag 08H5 (lemma-tor-amplitude-pullback), final application of the flat-model criterion

proof.text: By [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], the ordinary tensor complex in Step 6 has degree-$r$ term $B^r\otimes_{\mathcal O_U}G$, since $G[0]$ has only degree zero. For $r\notin[a,b]$ this term is zero: tensor with a fixed sheaf is additive, hence takes zero to zero, by [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. Its kernel and the image entering it are therefore zero, so its $r$-th cohomology sheaf $\ker(d^r)/\operatorname{im}(d^{r-1})$ is zero by [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Cohomology carries the isomorphism of Step 6 to an isomorphism, proving the requested vanishing for this arbitrary $G$ and $r$. Since $U$ was arbitrary, this proves the item.

proof_origin.place: Tag 08H5 (lemma-tor-amplitude-pullback), specialized to slice restriction, using Tag 08G1 (lemma-tor-amplitude). Expanded the categorical hypotheses of the existing bounded-flat-model theorem and the one-K-flat-factor tensor calculation.
